facebook.copy:
How do you know a roofer is legit?

Before you let anyone on your roof, ask for these. Any contractor worth hiring will hand them over without a fuss:

• A written contract that spells out the scope of work
• A certificate of insurance before work starts
• A payment schedule that doesn't ask for everything up front
• A manufacturer program you can look up yourself

Lucas Construction is an Owens Corning Preferred Contractor and installs Owens Corning Duration shingles. Look us up.

facebook.copy:
Four questions to ask before you hire a roofer

A good roofer won't mind being checked. Before you sign with anyone, ask:

• Can I see a written contract that spells out the scope of work?
• Can I see your certificate of insurance before work starts?
• What's the payment schedule? Be wary of anyone who wants everything up front.
• Which manufacturer program are you part of, and where can I look that up?

Our answers start here: Lucas Construction is an Owens Corning Preferred Contractor and installs Owens Corning Duration shingles. Ask us the rest anytime.

facebook.copy:
Cleaning gutters this weekend? Before you dump what you scoop out, take a look at it.

Leaves and twigs are normal. What's worth noticing is a gritty, sand-like layer in the bottom of the gutter or piled up at the downspout. Those are granules from the surface of your roof. A little is common. A lot of it is worth having a roofer look at before winter.

And be careful on that ladder.

facebook.copy:
Your gutters can tell you a lot about your roof

Fall is when most of us are up the ladder clearing leaves anyway, so it's a good time to look at a few other things while you're there:

• Gritty granules collecting in the gutter or at the downspout
• Roof edges that look curled or lifted
• Gutters that have started pulling away from the fascia
• Water stains or dark streaks below the gutter line

None of these tells you on its own what your roof needs. If you're seeing more than one, it's worth a conversation with a roofer before winter.

Lucas Construction is a roofing, siding, guttering, fascia and soffit contractor in Wentzville.

facebook.copy:
That "sand" in your gutters probably isn't sand.

If you're scooping out leaves this fall and find a gritty layer underneath, those are most likely granules off the surface of your roof. They're part of the roof's protective top layer, and every roof sheds some over time.

Finding a lot of them is a good reason to have a roofer take a look before winter, especially after a hailstorm. It doesn't automatically mean anything is wrong. It just means it's worth checking.
